definitions.meaning: The transfer of pollen from an anther to a stigma.
The fusion of the male gamete with the ovule, forming the start of a seed.
The tiny grains that carry the male gamete of a flowering plant.
The part of the stamen that makes and releases pollen.
The sticky tip of the carpel where pollen lands.
The stalk the pollen tube grows down, between stigma and ovary.
The base of the carpel that holds the ovules and becomes the fruit.
The structure inside the ovary that becomes the seed after fertilisation.
The tube a landed pollen grain grows down the style to reach the ovule.
What a fertilised ovule becomes: a young plant in a protective coat, with a food store.
The scattering of seeds away from the parent plant by wind, water, animals or explosion.

mechanismSteps: Pollination delivers: pollen grains travel from an anther to a stigma, carried by wind, water or animals (s1).
Fertilisation fuses: the pollen grows a tube down the style and the male nucleus fuses with the ovule (s2).
Dispersal scatters: the fertilised ovule becomes a seed that travels by wind, water, animals or exploding pods (s3).
The two events stay separate: delivery first, fusion second - landing on a stigma is not fusion (s4).
objectives: Describe pollination as the transfer of pollen from anther to stigma
Explain fertilisation as the fusion of the male gamete with the ovule
Name four seed dispersal methods and why dispersal helps
subject: science
title: Reproduction: pollination to seed

trap.explanation: The slip: The two words appear together in every story about flowers, so they merge into one event. The fix: Pollination is delivery: the male gamete must still fuse with the ovule for fertilisation. In class, replay the myth scene: freeze the moment the grain lands and ask what is still missing - the tube, the journey down the style, and the fusion itself.

workedExample: Test the merged-events claim on one landed grain. Step 1 (s1): the grain lands on the stigma, so transfer is complete and pollination has happened. Step 2 (s2): the pollen tube has only just started to grow, so the male nucleus has not met the ovule and no fusion has happened. The flower is pollinated but not fertilised, and the merged-events claim fails.
